sources.text:
Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump, and Russian President Vladimir Putin will hold historic three-way talks on Thursday at the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in Shenzhen, China. Here’s what you need to know:
The three leaders will hold a joint session together before separate one-on-one meetings later today.
Xi met Trump on the airport tarmac in Shenzhen on Wednesday, where Trump and Putin also shook hands ahead of the welcome banquet and leaders’ group photo.
The Chinese leader called for open trade, and both he and Putin criticised US economic sanctions.
Trump said he plans to discuss limiting nuclear weapons and bringing an end to the war in Ukraine. Analysts are not expecting major breakthroughs despite the unprecedented nature of the meeting.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese appeared in Wednesday’s APEC leaders’ group photo, though some distance from Putin in the back row. He is scheduled to meet Xi and Chinese Premier Li Qiang to lobby China to lift its 55 per cent tariffs on Australian beef exports.
We’ll bring you all the highlights from day two of the heavily choreographed event.

Historic moment - or just another photo op?
By
When Trump meets Xi and Putin, it could mark a pivot in world history – or become a quickly forgotten photo op.
Trump, who will test his reputation as an expert dealmaker in the trilateral meeting, has promoted his time with Xi and Putin — two of America’s leading rivals — as a chance to hash out rules for controlling nuclear arms and to start resolving the wars in Ukraine and Iran. Experts have kept expectations low for major breakthroughs.
The president said the advantage of meeting the two autocrats at the same time was that their countries work together.
The meeting is Trump’s third with XI Jinping this year.Getty Images
“They both like Trump. Now, what happens after me? That I can’t tell you,” Trump said in a Thursday interview with Fox News.

The view from New York and Washington
By
The New York Times describes President Xi Jinping’s decision to meet Trump at Shenzhen Airport yesterday as “unusual”.
“He did not come when Trump visited Beijing in May. But Trump made a point of going to Joint Base Andrews outside Washington to greet Xi in September, an uncommon move for a US president and the first time Trump had done so for a foreign visitor.”
“In effect, Xi returned the gesture,” the paper says, noting that Xi sent a lower-ranking official to meet Russia’s Vladimir Putin, who arrived earlier in the day.
China’s President Xi Jinping greeted Donald Trump with a hug after he walked down the stairs off Air Force One.Getty Images
The contrast underlined Xi’s efforts to balance relations with Russia and the US, the Times suggests, with Beijing’s strategic partnership with Moscow offset by its bigger economic ties to Washington.

Russia and China pledge “new level” of military ties
By
Russia and China have pledged to strengthen their military ties to build a world less dominated by the United States after presidents Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping met face to face on Wednesday.
The two countries will collaborate on projects to build aircraft, air defence and naval and space technologies, said Dmitry Shugayev, head of Russia’s service for military-technical co-operation, adding that they had reached a “new level” of partnership.
Chinese Navy personnel assemble to welcome the Russian missile cruiser Varyag to Qindao in July. The ship took part in a joint naval exercise with Chinese forces. Li Fengxiang/Xinhua via AP
Putin said both Moscow and Beijing were taking “constructive approaches to shaping a more equitable, multipolar world order”, in a veiled challenge to US dominance.
The Russian leader’s early arrival in Shenzhen allowed him to secure a one-on-one meeting with Xi.
8.17am
Trump brings the X factor
By
For all the anticipation leading up to this three-way summit, expectations for a major breakthrough are low.
Trump, Xi and Putin are coming to the table with different priorities. The Chinese leader wants to focus generally on world peace, Putin is looking for an off-ramp out of the war in Ukraine on favourable terms, and Trump would like to limit nuclear weapons.
Donald Trump pictured in Manila on Wednesday.Getty Images
The meeting is expected to be highly choreographed, with access tightly controlled. But at such a high-profile gathering, there is a certain degree of unpredictability about what Trump might do when the cameras are rolling.
Ukrainian and European leaders fear Trump might try to strike a deal with Putin on Ukraine. Taiwan worries that any move by the leaders could encourage China to put more pressure on the self-ruled island.
The summit may be scripted. Trump often isn’t.

Fried chicken diplomacy in Manila
By
Donald Trump’s love of fast food is well documented. One of the most memorable photos from his winning 2024 presidential campaign captured him wearing an apron and cooking French fries at a McDonald’s.
On Wednesday, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos jnr announced to a gathering of Asian leaders in Manila that he had ordered fried chicken from the famed Filipino chain Jollibee for Trump and his delegation as a late-night snack.
Marcos boasted that Jollibee is so popular that “we are very proud to say that we have surpassed KFC in the United States in terms of popularity.”
“Oh wow, fantastic,” said Trump, who has been known to dip into buckets of the US chain’s fried poultry.

Not one, but two “family photos” with Putin
By Lisa Visentin
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese also took part in the carefully choreographed gala group photo on Wednesday evening, standing in the back row next to Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, while Xi, Trump, Putin took centre stage.
For Putin, it was his first “family photo” with APEC leaders in nine years, with his last showing in Da Nang in Vietnam in 2017.
China’s President Xi Jinping poses with US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and other leaders at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.Getty Images
Albanese had been under political pressure at home to opt out of the photo if Putin was present as a protest against Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Both he and Carney indicated they ignored these calls out of respect for China’s role as host.
However, this will not be the last time Albanese is photographed with the Russian leader. He is due to appear in the official APEC group photo this morning.
7.29am
Trump to hold talks with Xi before three-way meeting
By Lisa Visentin
Before meeting Putin and Xi, Trump will hold separate bilateral talks with the Chinese president.
Xi is holding all of his sideline diplomatic meetings at Kylin Villa, a resort about a 20-minute drive away from the main APEC venue.
It will be the third time Trump has met with Xi this year, but the first occasion since the bruising midterm elections and the Nvidia scandal, injecting a potentially new dynamic into their fragile trade truce.
Loading
The downfall of Nvidia boss Jensen Huang over his affair with a businesswoman accused of links to Chinese intelligence, and suspected by US authorities of funnelling banned chips to China, will hang over the leaders’ talks even if not directly discussed.
Trump arrived on Xi’s turf this week with a fresh set of export controls aimed at further chocking China’s access to advanced chips. It has angered Beijing, which has accused Washington of fabricating a spy scandal as a pretext for imposing a technological blockade and has vowed to take countermeasures.
Before this summit, Trump and Putin last met face-to-face in Alaska in August last year, where they held bilateral talks to discuss the war in Ukraine.
This is the blockbuster day, where the grunt work of the summit’s trade focus will be overshadowed by the unprecedented spectacle of a trilateral meeting between Chinese leader Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The meeting, scheduled for 2.30pm local time (5.30pm AEDT), will mark the first time in history the leaders of the US, China and Russia have sat down for face-to-face talks. No agenda has been publicly confirmed, but Putin is widely expected to use the talks to push for a favourable end to Russia’s war in Ukraine. In a speech at the summit on Wednesday, Putin said he anticipated “big potential benefits” from the three-way meeting.
The world got an early preview of the images that will come from Thursday’s talks when the men greeted each other with smiles and handshakes while waiting for a group photo at a gala dinner on Wednesday evening.

sources.news_title: ‘Love your enemies’: ‘Big three’ arrive for historic summit in Shenzen not Wuhan
sources.text:
by WorldTribune Staff, November 18, 2026 — Real World News
Matthew 5:43-45
43 “You have heard that it was said, ‘Love your neighbor[a] and hate your enemy.’ 44 But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, 45 that you may be children of your Father in heaven. He causes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.”
U.S. President Donald Trump will meet on Thursday, Nov. 19, with Chinese Communist Party leader Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin in an historic first.
The meeting is taking place on the sidelines of the APEC conference in Shenzhen, an area which is China’s answer to Silicon Valley, only much bigger.
Prior to Thursday’s gathering, the leaders of the United States, Russia, and China had never sat down or met together in a trilateral format in modern history. The three met for a photo-op on Wednesday ahead of Thursday’s session.
Some analysts suggest the meeting could establish communication channels, quiet but significant side deals, or serve as a prelude to further talks such as next month’s G20 summit in Miami.
Regardless of the real outcome in private, the meeting would be heavy on political and diplomatic optics for the world at large.
Not on the official agenda is what originated in Wuhan, China in 2019. The global pandemic killed millions, upended the first term of President Trump and is a topic the Chinese Communist Party does not discuss.
Trump aims to discuss nuclear disarmament. White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales said the president “will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous.”
Miles Yu, a China expert who worked on China policy in the first Trump Administration, told C-SPAN in an interview that the nuclear issue is “important. China has been developing a nuclear arsenal at a decent speed. It is pretty scary. The Soviet Union and even Russia today have legacy nuclear powers. They are stabilizing. There was a robust disarmament arrangement between the Soviet Uninon and Russia and the U.S. We want to bring China in. China is playing hard to get. In the first Trump Administration, we invited China to disarmament talks. China did not come and we had an empty chair there.”
[See Yu’s interview with C-SPAN in full below.]
China has insisted that Russia and the U.S. should first reduce their much larger arsenals” before any trilateral discussions can begin.
Xi’s priority “is a successful gathering and presenting the image of stabilization of relations among great powers. China will focus on the symbolism rather than specific deals reached,” Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center in Washington, told Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty.
Putin stands to gain the most among the three leaders even if the summit achieves little of substance accoding to Tsiporah Fried, a visiting senior fellow at the Hudson Institute in Washington.
“It will help him restore his international standing and break out of the isolation that Russia has experienced. He can portray Russia as a great power negotiating the future of Ukraine, without having to think about losing on the battlefield,” she said.
Xi on Wednesday made a surprise appearance to greet Trump on the tarmac as he arrived in China — with the men shaking hands and hugging.
Xi rarely greets visiting foreign leaders when they land. He dispatched the fifth-ranking Communist Party official to meet Putin earlier Wednesday.
The Chinese president’s unusual gesture of respect reciprocated Trump’s greeting of Xi at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington in September. Trump’s in-person welcome was the first for the visiting foreign leader since 1962.

sources.news_title: Trump, Xi, and Putin Are Having a Trilateral Summit. But What’s on the Agenda?
sources.text:
The first-ever trilateral summit between U.S. President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese leader Xi Jinping is set for November 19 in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC summit. The agenda is unclear, though the White House claims the lead topic will be nuclear proliferation while Putin seems to want to discuss Ukraine.
Putin originally floated the idea of a trilateral meeting during a phone call with Trump in October. He sought the meeting to discuss ways to end the war in Ukraine, which is possibly suggestive of the effectiveness of Ukraine’s deep strikes within Russia hitting energy and other critical infrastructure. To underscore the point, Ukraine appears to have destroyed a significant portion of the Kerch bridge, which connects the disputed Crimea to Russian territory, in the last couple of days.
Meanwhile, the White House stated that Trump will use the trilateral meeting to focus on “the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous.”
The three countries are meeting nine months after the New START, the last of the bilateral strategic nuclear arms control agreement between the United States and Russia, expired in February this year. The Trump administration let the treaty expire rather than renew or replace it because Trump is keen on a broader pact that would also include China. Even during his first term, Trump had called for trilateral discussions on nuclear issues.
China has so far rejected the offer of nuclear talks, arguing that it has a considerably smaller nuclear arsenal compared to Russia and the U.S. and that it poses no threat. Most recently, China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson said, “China’s nuclear strength is by no means at the same level with that of the U.S. and Russia. It is neither fair, reasonable nor realistic to ask China to join the so-called trilateral nuclear disarmament negotiations at this stage.”
China undoubtedly has the fastest growing nuclear arsenal in the world and any effort at bringing China into an arms control process should be a welcome step. Therefore, if Trump is successful in having a focused discussion on nuclear issues in Shenzhen, it could be a good start.
But we should not expect any kind of agreement or statement regarding nuclear issues to come out of this trilateral. Normally, summits such as this are the culmination of significant negotiations, with leaders coming to sign agreements already reached between their respective bureaucracies. That has not happened, which suggests that this will be more of a photo-opportunity than a momentous diplomatic moment. That said, the trilateral could serve to kick-off negotiations, which itself would be a significant achievement. However, there is no indication that Xi has changed his mind on joining such negotiations.
Any progress on nuclear arms control talks will be in Australia’s interests too because China’s nuclear build-up, especially with no transparency or limits, could potentially trigger a nuclear arms race in the Pacific.
For its part, China has yet to indicate any issues of interest for the trilateral and therefore it is difficult to see what Beijing seeks to gain from this meeting. The trilateral summit will be more than a bit concerning if the three leaders end up discussing ideas like spheres of influence, though no such outcome will be lasting.
If the three countries were to reach a deal on Ukraine or Taiwan, that could also be potentially detrimental to regional and global security. Any such agreement would mostly end up being in favor of Russia and China, ignoring the basic tenets of international law. Reaching a deal on Ukraine without Kyiv being part of the discussions may lead to disastrous outcomes for both Ukraine and Europe, but also for the broader democratic community. It would set a bad precedent for China and other authoritarian states in carrying forward their regional territorial ambitions. Even though Trump indicated that he is not keen for the three to discuss Ukraine, media reports suggest that Trump will, in fact, talk Ukraine with Xi and Putin. One can understand how stressful a prospect that must be for Ukraine considering that Trump had earlier said he was fine with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy not being present at a potential meeting with Putin about the war.
On Taiwan, specifically, Trump needs to maintain U.S. commitments and move ahead with arms sales. Sacrificing Taiwan for a trade truce with China would be a horrible mistake. It would only embolden China to pursue such high-handedness while dealing with the U.S., Australia, and others in the rest of Indo-Pacific. China has already many times used economic coercion as leverage to achieve its strategic goals but it hasn’t often succeeded. It would be dangerous to alter that trend.
The best outcome for Australia, and the rest of the international community, will be that this trilateral summit is simply a photo-opportunity to let Trump have a sense of some achievement on the global scene, after a few bad weeks at home.

sources.news_title: Trump arrives in China focused on friendship, not spy scandal
sources.text:
Skip to content
Trump arrives in China focused on friendship, not spy scandal
Left unaddressed was the recent revelation that Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, had an extramarital affair with a business executive who U.S. intelligence agencies believe was spying for China.
SHENZHEN, China — President Donald Trump was welcomed to China on Wednesday with a warm embrace both figuratively and literally, as he arrived for a fraught visit shadowed by a major spy scandal that he seemed determined to ignore.
Upon landing in Shenzhen, a bustling technology center, for a series of meetings, Trump was greeted at the airport by President Xi Jinping of China, who hugged him on a red carpet as a colorfully dressed crowd waved flowers and flags and chanted “warm welcome” in Mandarin.
The visit, however, may have a see-no-evil, hear-no-evil quality because Trump has said he does not intend to raise the biggest China spy scandal of recent years, one that has upended one of America’s technology giants and pitted members of his own administration against each other. Instead, Trump prioritized a show of friendship amid the allegations of espionage.
Trump reveled in the pageantry of the moment as he joined Xi for a banquet dinner that opened the annual meeting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, a group of 21 major economies in the region. The two leaders toasted future prosperity and looked forward to meeting separately Thursday as well as together with President Vladimir Putin of Russia in a much-anticipated trilateral summit.
Xi’s decision to personally welcome Trump at the airport was a rare act by the Chinese leader. He did not do so when Trump visited Beijing in May. But Trump made a point of traveling to Joint Base Andrews outside Washington to greet Xi in September, an uncommon move for a U.S. president and the first time Trump had done so for a foreign visitor.
So, Xi returned the gesture Wednesday. “China is a nation of etiquette with a tradition of reciprocity,” Xi said, according to Chinese state media.
By contrast, Xi sent lower-level officials to greet Putin and other regional leaders arriving for the summit meeting, as is customary.
Still, Xi met separately with Putin for more than two hours in advance of the three-way meeting planned for Thursday, and he hailed the Chinese-Russian relationship as “steadfast as a rock through wind and rain.”
The two encounters underscored Xi’s efforts to balance relations with Russia and the United States. While Russia has become a close partner in recent years and Xi and Putin have developed a bond over dozens of meetings, China has a far more extensive and important economic relationship with the United States.
The atmosphere at the summit with other leaders was sometimes tense. Xi barely offered a smile to Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi of Japan, with whom he is in a bitter, yearlong diplomatic spat. Trump and Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada, who have an uneasy relationship as they tussle over trade, had their first in-person meeting of the year. Days earlier, Carney angered the Trump administration by repeating that he would look elsewhere, including to China, if Trump did not lift tariffs on Canada’s auto exports.
Left unaddressed was the recent revelation that Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, had an extramarital affair with a business executive who U.S. intelligence agencies believe was spying for China. The executive, Alice Huang, who is not related, worked for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center firm and was suspected of gathering intelligence for Beijing.
Jensen Huang resigned under pressure and Trump’s senior advisers have been squabbling over administration policy on chip exports that could benefit China. The administration announced earlier this week new rules meant to restrict remote access to advanced chips and servers that could help develop Chinese artificial intelligence.
Scott Bessent, the treasury secretary, has blamed Howard Lutnick, the commerce secretary, for resisting restrictions on chip sales. Bessent and Lutnick are both accompanying Trump on his Asia trip, though they were seen standing apart.
The Nvidia scandal has put Trump on the defensive because of his close relationship with Huang, who joined the president’s trip to China in May. Trump has denied being told about the matter, despite reporting by The New York Times that he was informed at least twice, including en route to China in May. He has said he does not know if Alice Huang was a spy and urged Jensen Huang to fight for his job. Even after Jensen Huang’s resignation, Trump voiced support for his reinstatement.
This is not the first time Trump has opted not to confront Xi with allegations of Chinese interference in the sensitive U.S. matters. In a primetime address to the nation in July, Trump accused China of hacking or purchasing U.S. voter rolls, but then said nothing about it publicly when he hosted Xi for a lavish state visit at the White House in September.
Although Trump once regularly lashed out at China over its trade practices, he has become more intent over the past year on forging closer ties between the world’s two largest economies. “We have a very good relationship with China, and you don’t want to insult them,” he said before leaving the United States.
Trump arrived in China after a stop in Manila, Philippines, for the annual meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, or ASEAN. He met with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. of the Philippines, who engaged in some fast-food diplomacy with Trump, who is known for his taste for greasy meals.
Marcos said he sent some fried chicken to Trump at his hotel the night before from Jollibee, a chain that is considered a national treasure in the Philippines. “Since you’re strapped for time, I thought a taste of Manila might be good,” he said. Trump did not say whether he ate the food.
He did, however, make a point of paying a visit to Marcos’ mother, Imelda Marcos, 97, the former first lady of the Philippines, who got to know Trump at New York parties in the 1990s.
“Welcome to the Philippines,” she told Trump. She handed him a gift and blew him a kiss as he walked away with her son.
“She’s always the most beautiful,” Trump said.
While Trump failed to sign a trade deal with Thailand that had been expected to be finalized during his stop in Manila, he announced that he did unexpectedly reach a trade agreement with the Philippines. “We didn’t know that was going to take place, but it took place very quickly and it’s a magnificent deal for both,” he said.
Marcos’ office later said the deal would cover energy and food security, without providing further details. Trump said on social media that the deal would benefit American farmers.
There was no such accord between Trump and Carney after their tense encounter in Shenzhen later in the day. In a statement, Carney’s office said the two leaders “discussed the work underway to reach a mutually beneficial trade agreement” but offered no further details.
Much attention was focused on Trump’s meeting with Xi and Putin on Thursday. The White House said Trump will also meet separately with Putin, their first get-together since a much-ballyhooed Alaska summit failed to produce an agreement to end the war in Ukraine.
Putin arrived in Asia with a show of force. Even as he landed in Shenzhen, Russian strategic nuclear bombers landed in Vietnam. It was the first time that Russian strategic nuclear bombers had deployed to Vietnam since the Soviet era and served as a reminder before the trilateral talks that Moscow remains the world’s largest nuclear power.

sources.news_title: TRUMP HOLDS COURT WITH XI AND PUTIN AT APEC AS ADMINISTRATION DECLARES: 'THIS IS NOT A CYBERATTACK'
sources.text:
President Donald J. Trump landed in Shenzhen, China, Tuesday and immediately took control of the APEC leaders' summit, sitting beside Xi Jinping and receiving a direct handshake approach from Vladimir Putin while his administration back home crushed the emerging narrative that America was under some kind of coordinated cyber siege.
The 47th President arrived at the communist stronghold after a day of red-carpet treatment in Manila, where Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. rolled out an honor guard, a cannon salute, and even a late-night Jollibee fried chicken run to welcome the leader of the free world.
No Cyber Bogeyman
Back in Manila, Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered the kind of straight talk Americans have been starving for since the Biden years of whispered leaks and anonymous-source chaos. Addressing the recent spate of airline, technical, and banking outages that had the legacy media breathlessly speculating about foreign hackers, Rubio was unambiguous.
"There is zero evidence whatsoever," Rubio said, adding there is "no indication of malign actors."
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton was even more direct: "This is not a cyberattack." The incidents, Rubio explained, are unrelated and trace back to patching vulnerabilities. Microsoft had nothing to do with the FAA. The FAA had nothing to do with the banks. "We are not under systematic attack," Rubio stated flatly.
Trump, Xi, and Putin in One Room
While Democrats fumbled for a new scare tactic, Trump was doing what he does best: showing up in person and dominating the room. Air Force One touched down in Shenzhen at 4:42 p.m. China time, and by 5:04 p.m., Xi Jinping was greeting Trump as a band played "The Star-Spangled Banner" and a multicolored military flyover streaked across the sky.
The family photo moment told the real story. As leaders filed into Xiangmi Hall—35 round tables set with pink roses awaiting them—Trump was the only leader who stopped to face the cameras as "America the Beautiful" played. When Putin entered, the Russian president made a point of approaching Trump directly for a handshake before the photo. Xi entered last, as protocol demands, but the visual belonged to Trump.
Before the banquet, the White House confirmed Trump held meetings at the Langham hotel with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. Three nations, three leaders, one American president doing the heavy lifting.
Philippines First
Earlier in the day, Trump inspected troops alongside Marcos at the presidential palace in Manila and cited the "bond formed in blood" between the two nations—a reference to the shared sacrifice of World War II and the defense of the Pacific. He also discussed Venezuela's 48-minute war, Iran, and defense arms sales, making clear that America's allies get the real deal, not empty promises.
Marcos toasted Trump's health in a Christmas-decorated ballroom, and Trump recalled General Douglas MacArthur's gold baton. The message was unmistakable: America's presence in the Pacific is not negotiable.
Domestic Calm Amid Media Panic
Rubio also dismissed the dirty-bomb threat chatter targeting Washington as nothing to worry about and confirmed that President Trump is serious about engaging North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. That's what leadership looks like—engaging adversaries from a position of strength, not hiding behind teleprompters and basement videos.
The White House called a lid at 9:34 p.m. local time, capping a day of diplomacy that saw Trump bounce from palace honors to superpower summit theater without breaking stride. First Lady Melania Trump will welcome the White House Christmas Tree on November 23—an 18-foot concolor fir from Wisconsin delivered by a 10-year Army veteran.
Patriots, ask yourselves: when was the last time an American president had Xi greeting him on the tarmac and Putin walking across the room to shake his hand—while his own intelligence chiefs calmly told the press there's no cyber bogeyman? The answer is never. This is what winning looks like.

sources.news_title: Trump, Putin and Xi meet in Shenzhen ahead of first trilateral summit
Ukraine Has a Problem: Kyiv and Europe Fear Putin Will Talk Trump Into Lifting More Sanctions on Russia When They Meet in China
sources.text:
On November 18, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin arrived in China ahead of a scheduled meeting with President Xi Jinping.
The three world leaders are set to hold trilateral discussions on Thursday on the sidelines of an economic summit in Shenzhen, China.
The three will reportedly discuss a wide range of topics, including nuclear disarmament and, most importantly, the ongoing war in Ukraine.
However, as large-scale Russian drone and missile attacks against Ukraine continue, Russia appears uninterested in ending the war, which has been ongoing for almost five continuous years.
It remains to be seen whether Thursday’s trilateral discussions will produce any tangible results.
Trilateral Talks in China
At 6 a.m. local time, President Trump arrived in China, where Xi Jinping personally greeted him, reminiscent of how the Chinese president was greeted when he arrived in the U.S. in September. Four hours earlier, Vladimir Putin arrived in China.
The Russian head of state held bilateral talks with Xi Jinping on November 18, ahead of the trilateral discussions with Trump.
The two discussed several topics, including economic priorities such as energy, finance, and AI.
According to some sources, they also discussed possible settlements to the war in Ukraine, although no details have been shared yet.
On Monday, President Trump said he was hoping to discuss nuclear disarmament and the war in Ukraine with Putin and Xi Jinping. President Zelenskyy is notably absent from the meetings, as are any representatives or heads of state from the UK or the European Union.
The meeting between the three leaders has been criticized as a “Yalta-2.0” meeting, wherein powerful heads of state decide the fate of smaller countries.
According to the Associated Press, Trump plans to hold a separate meeting with Putin on Thursday in addition to the trilateral discussions.
This would mark the first one-on-one meeting between Trump and Putin since the discussions in Anchorage, Alaska, last year, which likewise failed to produce any substantial results, much to Russia’s bitter disappointment.
Although previous meetings have failed to bring the war to an end, Trump told reporters he was confident that recent developments have created an opening to resolve the conflict. “I think it’s very close to getting it done,” he said. “We’re going to have a good meeting on that.”
Does Russia Really Want Peace?
Some cynical observers have blamed Ukraine, particularly Zelenskyy, for refusing to compromise on any of its ambitious war aims.
However, Russia is equally, if not more, responsible for prolonging the war for almost five years.
Moscow has remained firm in its ambitious war goals: the disarmament and neutrality of Ukraine, and the recognition of its annexed territories, even territories that it does not fully control.
So far, Russia has refused any proposal that falls short of these two demands.
Last week, as Trump’s envoys sought to mediate negotiations between Kyiv and Moscow, Russia reportedly submitted a list of demands to the U.S. The demands, according to The New York Times, include a call for NATO to pull its troops back to positions that it held in 1997, before the alliance expanded to Russia’s borders.
Russia submitted similar demands in 2022, right before it invaded Ukraine.
While Trump and Zelenskyy have been trying to broker a ceasefire, Russia has continuously rejected any proposal to freeze the front lines that does not also meet Moscow’s main demands.
The Kremlin believes any temporary pauses will only help Ukraine rebuild its defensive forces and ultimately prolong the war. “We have repeatedly said that we oppose a ceasefire that would give the Ukrainians a breathing space,” said Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov. Instead, the Kremlin demands a “comprehensive settlement” that addresses all of the underlying causes of the war, including NATO expansion and Ukrainian territorial disputes.
Europe Left Out of the Table
While Russia talks about a new “security architecture” in Europe, the EU and the UK have been largely left out, much to their chagrin.
During the U.S.-brokered talks between Russian and Ukrainian delegates in Abu Dhabi last week, European diplomats tried to join the discussions, but Russia promptly rejected them.
Russian officials have often stated that they have a low opinion of European officials.
In response to statements by Ursula von der Leyen and EU diplomat Kaja Kallas, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov criticized the EU for its “dead-end way of thinking.” Lavrov added that “At least with the Americans, we are having substantive discussions based on real facts, including the situation on the ground and the root causes of this conflict.” European officials are hoping to deploy ground troops to Ukraine once a ceasefire is reached, a position that the Kremlin has repeatedly said is unacceptable.
European and Ukrainian officials are worried that Putin will convince Trump to lift further sanctions against Russia, providing a much-needed windfall for the Russian economy.
Last month, the American president signed an executive order exempting Russia from the sanctions Congress imposed earlier.
Washington also entered into a trade deal with Moscow to import Russian diesel fuel to lower gas prices in the U.S. Ukraine and Europe saw the deal as a stab in the back from Trump, who has often been criticized for trying to form a personal relationship with Putin.
It is currently unclear what Thursday’s discussions will bring. Based on previous talks, however, it is unlikely that any substantial deals will be reached.
About the Author: Isaac Seitz
Isaac Seitz, a Defense Columnist, graduated from Patrick Henry College’s Strategic Intelligence and National Security program. He has also studied Russian at Middlebury Language Schools and has worked as an intelligence Analyst in the private sector.

sources.news_title: Xi Greets Trump Personally in Shenzhen: Putin Gets a Different Welcome
sources.text:
When the leaders of the world’s three most powerful nations converge in one city, every gesture matters. Every handshake, every protocol decision, every subtle diplomatic signal reveals who holds the leverage – and who doesn’t. With the first-ever trilateral meeting between the United States, China, and Russia set for Thursday in Shenzhen, the entire world is watching to see whether America can still command the room.
What happened on that tarmac Wednesday afternoon answered the question before the meeting even started.
From the Daily Wire:
Chinese President Xi Jinping broke with diplomatic precedent on Wednesday by personally greeting President Donald Trump with an embrace as he arrived in Shenzhen, China, ahead of a three-way meeting involving Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Xi waited on the tarmac to welcome Trump, marking an unusual gesture by the Chinese leader, who did not personally greet the American president during his previous visit to Beijing in May.
President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping shared a cheek-to-cheek hug in a rare airport welcome in Shenzhen.
Both leaders are set to meet Russia’s Vladimir Putin later in the week for an unprecedented summit. https://t.co/sileAS8yZi https://t.co/WqpzNfuPtl
— Bloomberg (@business) November 18, 2026
Pretty remarkable. And honestly? It tells you everything about how much China respects the man occupying the Oval Office right now. Xi Jinping doesn’t do spontaneous. Every move Beijing’s top man makes is calculated, deliberate, and saturated with meaning. The full production – flag-waving crowds, performers in colorful costumes, people chanting “warm welcome” in Mandarin, an actual red carpet – none of that was improvised. It was a message, broadcast to every capital on the planet.
What Putin didn’t get
Here’s where it gets interesting. Vladimir Putin touched down in Shenzhen earlier that same day. His welcoming committee? A lower-ranking Chinese official. No embrace. No fanfare. No spectacle.
Xi later praised the China-Russia relationship as “steadfast as a rock through wind and rain.” Warm words. But diplomatic theater doesn’t lie. China does significantly more business with the United States than with Russia, and Xi understands exactly where his priorities need to be.
Trump set this dynamic in motion back in September when he personally traveled to Joint Base Andrews to welcome Xi during the Chinese leader’s state visit to Washington. That show of respect just got repaid – with interest. That’s not weakness. That’s leverage, deployed with precision.
A historic meeting ahead
The real substance arrives Thursday. The trilateral agenda includes nuclear weapons, Iran, Ukraine, and global security. Trump told reporters he believes peace in Ukraine is “very close,” and Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed the president is “serious” about a potential sit-down with North Korea’s Kim Jong Un.
The foreign policy establishment spent years lecturing Americans that personal diplomacy with adversaries was naive and reckless. Meanwhile, the most powerful authoritarian leader on earth just gave an American president honors he wouldn’t extend to his own closest ally. Not through appeasement. Not through apology tours. Through strength – the only currency that buys respect on the world stage.
Key Takeaways
- Xi broke diplomatic precedent by personally greeting Trump – a gesture he pointedly denied Putin.
- Trump’s strength-first diplomacy is earning visible respect from America’s foremost rivals.
- Thursday’s unprecedented trilateral positions the U.S. at the center of global power negotiations.
- Personal leadership, not bureaucratic consensus, is driving real diplomatic results abroad.
Sources: Daily Wire, NPR, Reuters

sources.news_title: President Trump plans separate talks with Vladimir Putin alongside their meeting with Xi Jinping in China
sources.text:
SHENZHEN, China — When President Donald Trump meets on Thursday with China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, it could mark a pivot in world history — or become a quickly forgotten photo op.
Trump, who will test his reputation as an expert dealmaker in the trilateral meeting, has promoted his time with Xi and Putin — two of America’s leading rivals — as a chance to hash out rules for controlling nuclear arms and to start resolving the wars in Ukraine and Iran. Experts have kept expectations low for major breakthroughs.
The president said the advantage of meeting the two autocrats at the same time was because their countries work together.
“They both like Trump. Now, what happens after me? That I can’t tell you,” Trump said in a Thursday interview with Fox News.
Trump plans to have a separate one-on-one meeting with Xi — his third substantial meeting with him this year — right before the trilateral. He also added a separate sit-down with Putin to his schedule, marking the first time that the leaders have held talks since their discussions in Alaska last year that failed to broker a deal to ease Russia’s war in Ukraine.
Trump has frequently boasted of his rapport with Putin, even as relations between the U.S. and Ukraine appear to have cratered recently. Trump rejected new Russia sanctions, while Kyiv was undermined by disruptions in satellite support for its drones during the war.
Along for the trip — but so far keeping a low profile — is Elon Musk, whose company SpaceX has intermittently throttled the military-grade Starshield satellite system used by Ukraine for launching its drones and intercepting hits from Russia.
One meeting is unlikely to produce a breakthrough in nuclear talks
The trilateral is scheduled to occur after a session with leaders at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit on Thursday morning and is expected to be the capstone to Trump’s Asia trip that started Tuesday in the Philippines.
Trump has said he wants to talk to the leaders about their nuclear stockpiles. The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States, known as New START, expired in February, and Trump has said he wants “a new, improved and modernized” deal that includes China. But China has less motivation to accept limits given that its arsenal of more than 600 warheads is many times smaller than the more than 5,000 warheads believed to be in each of the U.S. and Russian stockpiles.
Daryl Kimball, executive director of the Arms Control Association, said that Trump’s showmanship could at best start a process that would eventually lead to a sustained set of talks for reducing nuclear arsenals.
“We need more than diplomatic theater and photo opportunities between Xi, Putin, and Trump at APEC,” Kimball said. “And one meeting will not likely produce dramatic breakthroughs.”
Trump told Fox News in his interview that “it’s a very hard thing to do” to ask a leader to reduce nuclear stockpiles.
Trump boasts about his relationships. But the ties between Xi and Putin are stronger.
Putin’s foreign affairs adviser Yuri Ushakov told reporters that Putin, Trump and Xi would likely touch on the war in Ukraine, though the agenda was not fully set. Trump has said he wants to discuss that war — as well as the conflict in Iran.
His ambitions recall an era of great power politics when wealthier countries felt entitled to decide the fate of seemingly lesser nations. Trump is negotiating with China and Russia without the involvement of Ukraine — or countries like Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Japan and South Korea that also have stakes in the outcome of any talks.
The U.S. president has openly pursued a Nobel Peace Prize even as he took military action against Venezuela and Iran. He also threatened earlier this year to take Greenland by force from Denmark, a gambit that led to an agreement for the construction of U.S. military bases.
Trump has long believed that his ability to create personal connections gives him a diplomatic edge. Xi appealed to his ego on Wednesday by greeting Air Force One on the airport tarmac, as the two leaders turned their handshake into a one-armed hug.
But Trump does not appear to always have the same deep relationship based on common interests that Xi and Putin share. For all the compliments the U.S. president has showered on the two autocrats, the warmth has not always been mutually effusive.
On Wednesday at APEC, Xi greeted Putin by calling him “my old friend.” The Russian leader responded by declaring Xi to be his “dear friend.” China has helped to economically support Russia after its 2022 invasion of Ukraine, providing Putin with a financial lifeline after the U.S. and its allies imposed new sanctions.
“China-Russia relations have remained steadfast through storms while taking a long-term view,” Xi said to Putin. “They have brought greater stability and certainty to a world marked by intertwined changes and turbulence.”
The pair discussed the war in Ukraine during their talks and Trump’s envoys who are trying to bring the conflict to an end, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian state news agency RIA Novosti.
By contrast, when Xi came to the White House for a state visit in September, he was far more restrained with Trump, saying that they had built a “personal rapport and stayed in touch.” Trump and Xi plan to meet a total of four times this year, with their final time together coming in December at the G20 summit being held at the Trump National Doral Golf Club in Florida.
Conflicts on AI and trade also hang over the meetings
While Trump views his relationship with China as a positive, it has not necessarily resulted in meaningful changes between the world’s two largest economies. China continues to run large trade surpluses with the rest of the world, while the U.S. has almost equally large trade deficits.
And the race between the U.S. and China to master artificial intelligence has grown tense over the past two weeks. Trump ally Jensen Huang resigned last week as the CEO of Nvidia after confessing to an extramarital affair with a woman, Alice Huang, whose company helped to give China access to the company’s advanced computer chips used to develop AI models. Beijing has denied that Alice Huang was a Chinese government agent.
Trump held off on imposing tougher restrictions on China’s ability to access the chips, suggesting that he did not want to insult China and aggravate relations.
Before APEC, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer met with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng.
The U.S. officials said afterward that China had not fully honored its commitments made last year in a Trump-Xi meeting to buy more U.S. agricultural products and loosen restrictions on the sale of rare earth minerals needed for electronics.
The trade truce between the U.S. and China reached last year after dueling tariff hikes is set to expire by January 10 next year.
Trump officials have dangled the possibility of opening up highly sanctioned trade with Russia as an incentive for ending hostilities in Ukraine, and Trump has frequently demonstrated that he sees trade as a foreign policy tool.
Meanwhile, both China and Russia have used trade to support Iran, even during the U.S. war on that country which has pushed up energy prices and reduced global economic growth.
Associated Press writer Will Weissert in Washington contributed to this report.

sources.news_title: What Trump, Putin and Xi want from their historic meeting
sources.text:
What Trump, Putin and Xi want from their historic meeting
The world's three most powerful nuclear leaders are preparing to make history by meeting for the first time.
The historic summit between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin will take place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in China's southern city of Shenzhen.
But analysts are sceptical anything concrete will come from the highly anticipated talks.
So what might a meeting between these men achieve? And why hold a summit if a firm result is not expected?
What is likely to be discussed?
China and Russia have not confirmed any talking points for the summit but have expressed lofty aspirations for "in-depth exchanges" that would be symbolic and significant.
It means most of what is known about potential agenda items comes from the White House, which has identified key issues including:
- nuclear non-proliferation;
- the wars in Ukraine and Iran;
- trade and;
- artificial intelligence
Why is nuclear a key issue?
America has a clear goal of forming a new arms agreement with Russia and China.
Russia currently has the world's largest arsenal of nuclear warheads, followed closely by the United States, with China's rapidly expanding cache sitting significantly behind.
The agreement between America and Russia capping strategic nuclear arsenals, called the New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (New START), lapsed in February this year.
The United Nations has urged both sides to agree to a new framework without delay, but Mr Trump has been reluctant to sign a new agreement unless it also included China.
A White House spokeswoman said Mr Trump would use the meeting to discuss a reduction of nuclear weapons in the world.
"This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous," said White House representative Olivia Wales.
However, experts told the ABC they do not expect much to be decided on nuclear arsenals.
China has historically railed against being part of the agreement and views its arsenal as significantly less than Russia's and America's.
When asked whether Beijing would discuss the idea, foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said "the three presidents will have an in-depth exchange of views on safeguarding world peace and enabling strategic stability in major-country relations" but would not provide specific details.
Russia, too, has been vague on what it would like to discuss at the summit, with Kremlin foreign policy aide Yury Ushakov instead pointing to the "significance and symbolism of this meeting".
"It has been agreed that [this meeting] should be structured in the spirit of the mutual understanding and alliance between our three countries during World War II, with an emphasis on our countries' cooperation in the establishment of the United Nations," he told reporters.
What could the meeting mean for Ukraine and Iran wars?
The wars in Iran and Ukraine may also be on the agenda.
There have been concerns Mr Trump could use the meeting to discuss an end to the conflict in Ukraine without Kyiv in the room.
When speaking to reporters about the meeting earlier this week, the US president said he was ready to discuss his "favourite subject, Ukraine", which the Kremlin also supports.
It could be an uncomfortable moment for China, which has claimed neutrality in the war despite its close ties with Russia.
NATO allies have accused Beijing of providing material support for the war with the export of dual-use goods, though China has consistently maintained it is not supplying Moscow.
It is unclear what role the superpower would play in potentially bringing the war to an end.
China's assistance in the US and Israeli-led war in Iran may be a little more clearer, with Mr Trump potentially turning to Beijing, an ally of Tehran, to help end that conflict or to pressure Iran to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Beijing is the main buyer of Iran's oil and its largest trading partner, and it also wants to see an end to the conflict.
But it is unlikely to want to embroil itself in a protracted conflict and has previously avoided wading into ceasefire negotiations.
What will Xi, Trump and Putin get out of this?
Despite low expectations for any key deliverables from this summit, each leader is coming into this with their own goals and ambitions.
"This summit … demonstrates the multi-polarity of international politics today," said Wi Xinbo, director at the Center for American Studies at Fudan University.
"This means that there is no longer a unipolar world, and the US has to respect and recognise the role and importance of China and Russia in international affairs."
Mr Xi, who has spent years building his image and position as a serious geopolitical and diplomatic powerbroker, hopes to emerge as the only person able to bring together these three countries together for a historic moment.
For Mr Trump, coming off bruising midterm elections, he will want to portray strength alongside other strongmen.
"Mr Trump gains a bit in being able to have a platform to demonstrate some deal-making, maybe advancing some talks on Ukraine, possibly nuclear arms control," said Han Shen Lin, China managing director for The Asia Group.
"But his pay-off depends more on actually producing a tangible result, which is [a] pretty high [ask]."
But some analysts suggest the biggest winner from the sit-down will be Russia, with Mr Putin to be recognised as a major diplomatic player, not a pariah, on the world stage.
"He will have achieved his return to the top table in global diplomacy without making any significant concessions on Ukraine or elsewhere," wrote Ryan Hass from the Brookings Institute.
A joint press conference or communique after the meeting is not expected, so readouts released by each country will be pored over for what happened behind closed doors.
Either way, a photo of the three most powerful nuclear powers in the world, talking together for the first time, will be one for the history books.

sources.news_title: Trump set to meet Putin in China for one-to-one meeting
sources.text:
Trump set to meet Putin in China for one-to-one meeting
US President Donald Trump is set to hold a separate meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in China in addition to a previously scheduled three-way summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, a US government official says.
It remained initially unclear exactly when the meeting would take place.
Trump and Putin were attending the official reception for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen on Wednesday evening.
There are a multitude of issues to discuss, Putin's foreign policy adviser Yuri Ushakov told Russian state television in advance of the APEC summit.
Trump and Putin last met in August 2025 in Anchorage in the US state of Alaska, where they discussed Russia's war against Ukraine.
Trump is endeavouring to act as a mediator to bring the war to an end but he has been repeatedly accused of being too close to Russia.
At the Alaska meeting Trump gave Putin a red carpet reception.
The two presidents have also spoken on the phone on several occasions.
In Shenzhen on Wednesday, the two were seen sharing a brief handshake and a few words at a photo opportunity, where they were placed either side of Xi, who was hosting the summit, and his wife.
Interfax said Trump and Putin did not have a substantive conversation.
Ushakov said the Putin-Trump meeting would take place after the APEC plenary session and that several members of the Russian and US delegations were expected to attend.
The Putin-Trump-Xi summit is a significant meeting from which many good results are expected, Ushakov said.
On Wednesday evening, he said the exact agenda was still being worked on but Ukraine should be the focus of these talks.
Trump had said he wanted to discuss nuclear disarmament with Putin and Xi.
Work is also under way on the summit's final document, Ushakov said.
Key points still need to be clarified.
"Intensive work under way so far," Ushakov said.
It is the first time that the heads of state of China, Russia and the United States are meeting for a summit.
Russian commentators had spoken of a new "G3 format".
APEC comprises the governments of 21 countries including the US, China and Russia.
It aims to promote free trade and economic co-operation in the Asia-Pacific region.

sources.news_title: Xi, Trump, Putin exchange greetings before historic China summit
sources.text:
The leaders of China, the United States and Russia exchanged greetings as they met in Shenzhen on Wednesday, a day before their history-making first formal trilateral summit in the Chinese city.
The agenda for Thursday’s meeting between presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin – which has raised fearsof a carve-up into new “spheres of influence” – was unclear, however.
And the three-way meeting was set to last “no more than an hour”, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian state media.
When Trump touched down in Shenzhen, Xi became the first Chinese paramount leader in decades to welcome a foreign leader as he arrived, mirroring the US President’s gesture at Joint Base Andrews in September.
Trump descended the stairs from his plane to be met by Xi, as well as renditions of both countries’ national anthems and fighter jets that flew overhead and left colourful vapour trails.
The pair strolled down a red carpet lined with people waving pom-poms, brandishing Chinese and US national flags, and shouting: “A warm welcome to you!”
A motorcade of dark limousines later carried Trump into the city, where the streets had been cleared of traffic, an AFP reporter observed.
Xi, Trump, Putin and other leaders attending the broader Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit then gathered for a welcome dinner, and the three briefly exchanged greetings before a group photo.
“I look forward to an in-depth exchange of views with you on major issues concerning China-US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global landscape, with the aim of advancing a constructive, strategically stable relationship between our two nations,” Xi told Trump, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua.
Sanctions ‘failed’: Putin
Washington had signalled that the Ukraine war – something Xi vehemently sees as not China’s problem – was not expected to be addressed in the trilateral meeting, before Trump said that it would.
The summit is expected to include discussions of the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.
Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile.
Earlier on Wednesday, Putin struck a defiant tone on his war in Ukraine, saying Western sanctions provoked by the 2022 invasion had “failed”.
Addressing the Apec gathering, the Russian leader said he expected the trilateral summit to be “highly useful”.
“At a time when military-political risks are on the rise, what is desperately needed is unity rather than division... and dialogue rather than ultimatums,” Putin said.
The Russian leader has been largely shunned by the West since his 2022 offensive in Ukraine began, but has found an audience with Trump.
However, “full-scale” talks solely between Putin and Trump are unlikely to take place during their visits to China, Moscow said, according to Russian state media.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, also in Shenzhen, said sanctions would “continue to increase as long as this war goes on”.
Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga, speaking to reporters in Kyiv, said he hoped Xi and Trump would put “pressure on Russia to end the war”.
Kim incoming?
Putin and Xi met, their fifth tête-à-tête this year, including one by video link. The two men have long touted their strong personal friendship.
Xi urged yet closer ties with Moscow, saying the nations should “leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between the two countries’ governments, legislative bodies, militaries and political parties”.
Trump came to China from the Philippines, where a day earlier he met fellow leaders of the Quad – Australia, Japan and India – for the first time in his second term.
The grouping is broadly aimed at counterbalancing China’s regional influence.
Trump has also floated the possibility of meeting Kim Jong Un in China, saying the North Korean leader “would like” to meet, although there has been no confirmation from Pyongyang.
Trump was in the Philippines for a summit of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) where there were protests against a US supply chain initiative.
The spectre of Trump’s ongoing tariff blitz has loomed large over his recent travels.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday slammed what he called a “countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism” while touting Beijing’s own expanding trade with Asean.
On Tuesday, a combative Trump doubled down, saying the United States would catch China in rare-earths production “within 10 months”.

sources.news_title: Trump, Xi and Putin Gather at APEC Gala in China Ahead of Historic Three-Way Summit on Global Security
sources.text:
President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin exchanged greetings during a formal dinner in Shenzhen on Wednesday, ahead of unprecedented trilateral talks expected to address nuclear weapons, Ukraine and international security.
By yourNEWS Media Newsroom
President Donald Trump joined Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin at a formal Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation gala dinner Wednesday, Nov. 18, in Shenzhen, China, bringing the leaders of three major nuclear powers together ahead of a highly anticipated trilateral summit scheduled for Thursday.
The gathering took place at the Shenzhen International Communication Centre, where Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, welcomed visiting leaders attending the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting. Trump and Putin shook hands and exchanged brief remarks as Xi stood nearby, marking a significant public encounter before their planned discussions on international security and diplomatic relations.
Video footage of the reception showed the three presidents greeting one another before taking their positions for a group photograph with other participating leaders. The encounter occurred during a broader diplomatic gathering rather than a separate meeting exclusively involving the United States, China and Russia.
According to The Associated Press, the dinner followed a series of diplomatic meetings in which Xi emphasized international trade cooperation, while Putin criticized Western sanctions and economic restrictions.
Earlier Wednesday, Xi personally greeted Trump at Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport, welcoming the American president with a handshake and embrace as he arrived aboard Air Force One.
The unusual reception reflected a reciprocal diplomatic gesture following Trump’s decision to personally welcome Xi during the Chinese leader’s September visit to Washington.
Trump arrived from Manila, Philippines, where he had attended regional diplomatic meetings and discussed military and economic cooperation with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
Putin arrived in Shenzhen ahead of the American president and held a separate meeting with Xi before the evening reception.
During their bilateral discussions, the Chinese and Russian leaders reaffirmed their countries’ strategic relationship and discussed international economic and security issues.
The two governments have maintained extensive diplomatic and commercial ties despite Western sanctions against Russia following its invasion of Ukraine.
Xi also addressed business leaders attending APEC, urging greater economic cooperation and warning against protectionist measures that could weaken international trade.
The Chinese president’s remarks came amid continuing trade disputes involving tariffs, semiconductor technology, critical minerals and restrictions on sensitive exports.
According to Reuters reporting carried by GMA News, Trump and Putin exchanged greetings in Xi’s presence shortly before the banquet, with the three leaders subsequently joining the other heads of government for the official welcome dinner.
The occasion drew international attention because of the planned meeting Thursday involving all three presidents.
The trilateral discussions are expected to address nuclear arms control, the war in Ukraine and broader security relations among Washington, Beijing and Moscow.
The United States and Russia possess the world’s largest nuclear weapons arsenals, while China has continued expanding its nuclear capabilities.
Trump has expressed interest in negotiating arrangements that could limit nuclear weapons development among the three countries, although no formal agreement has been announced.
The war in Ukraine is another anticipated subject of discussion.
Russia’s military operations and Western economic sanctions have remained major points of disagreement between Moscow and Washington, while China has maintained diplomatic and economic relations with Russia.
The United States has also sought cooperation from Beijing in efforts to encourage negotiations over the conflict.
According to the Los Angeles Times, Wednesday’s dinner brought the three leaders together alongside other regional heads of government before their scheduled summit.
The diplomatic gathering occurred as Washington and Beijing continued negotiating economic issues involving tariffs, rare earth minerals and American restrictions on advanced artificial intelligence processors.
China remains an important producer and processor of critical minerals used in electronics, military equipment and industrial manufacturing.
The United States has pursued agreements with other countries to diversify those supply chains while maintaining restrictions on certain advanced technologies.
Russia, meanwhile, has criticized Western financial sanctions and trade restrictions, arguing that countries should reduce their dependence on Western-controlled economic institutions.
The Shenzhen summit provides a forum for the three governments to discuss those disputes directly.
The broader APEC meeting includes representatives from 21 member economies and focuses on regional trade, investment, economic growth and cooperation.
South Korean President Lee Jae-myung also attended Wednesday’s welcome dinner, along with other leaders participating in the summit.
According to Seoul Economic Daily, Lee greeted Trump, Xi and Putin during the reception, which included a formal group photograph and cultural presentations.
Shenzhen, located in China’s southern Guangdong province near Hong Kong, is one of the country’s principal technology and manufacturing centers.
The city hosts major companies involved in telecommunications, electronics, electric vehicles and advanced manufacturing, making it a significant setting for discussions about economic competition and technological development.
Wednesday’s public interactions offered an opportunity for the leaders to exchange greetings before beginning substantive negotiations.
Although the dinner included a handshake between Trump and Putin and another public appearance by Trump and Xi, no diplomatic agreement was announced following the reception.

WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW
- Surprise Airport Embrace: Chinese President Xi Jinping personally welcomed President Donald Trump at Shenzhen Airport on Wednesday, November 18, surprising observers with a handshake and hug as Trump stepped off Air Force One.
- Rare Diplomatic Gesture: Xi’s unusual appearance reciprocated Trump’s personal welcome in Washington in September, highlighting an effort to strengthen relations between the two leaders.
- Elaborate Chinese Welcome: Trump received a red-carpet reception featuring cheering performers, patriotic music, and a military flyover as China hosted the annual APEC conference.
- Historic Three-Way Summit Ahead: Trump, Xi, and Russian President Vladimir Putin are scheduled to meet Thursday for unprecedented trilateral talks addressing nuclear disarmament and international conflicts. Trump and Xi are also expected to discuss ongoing trade disputes and rare-earth export restrictions.
President Trump received an unusually personal welcome in Shenzhen on Wednesday when Chinese President Xi Jinping appeared on the tarmac to greet him. The two leaders shook hands and hugged before a historic trilateral summit scheduled for Thursday with Russian President Vladimir Putin, as reported by The New York Post.
Xi rarely meets visiting foreign leaders as they arrive, making the tarmac appearance a notable gesture of respect. Earlier Wednesday, an official ranked fifth in the Communist Party greeted Putin at Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport.
When Trump traveled to Beijing in May, Xi sent his vice president to welcome the American president. This time, Xi was waiting personally as Trump stepped onto Chinese soil, offering a striking opening to a visit packed with diplomacy and pageantry.

Trump arrived in Shenzhen, described as a Chinese boomtown just north of Hong Kong, after making a stop in the Philippines. He traveled to China for the annual APEC conference, which brings together leaders from 21 Pacific Rim economies.
Hundreds of performers lined the red carpet while waving flowers and chanting “enthusiastic warm welcome” in Mandarin. The elaborate reception also included a military flyover, which Trump applauded, along with a performance of the United States national anthem.
The ceremonial treatment continued into the evening as Trump arrived for an APEC banquet. Classical musicians performed “America the Beautiful” while the assembled leaders prepared for a dinner that kept the American president in a prominent position.
Xi gave Trump the place of honor beside him during a group photograph. At the banquet, Xi also seated Trump on his side of the head table, extending the public display of respect that began with the surprise airport greeting.
Putin approached Trump and shook his hand before the meal. Xi opened the banquet by calling for the preservation of “the Asia-Pacific miracle of rapid economic growth.”
The major diplomatic event will come Thursday with the first trilateral meeting involving the leaders of China, Russia and the United States. Trump said as he left Washington on Monday that the talks would focus on nuclear disarmament and ways the three powers might cooperate on major international conflicts.
Those discussions are expected to include the US war with Iran and efforts to end the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Trump has repeatedly emphasized his desire to maintain warm personal relationships with both Xi and Putin as a way to advance American interests and address global problems.
Trump also said he might raise the scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy seducing ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang joined Trump during the president’s trip to Beijing earlier this year, though Trump expressed concern that pressing the issue could insult China.
Before the trilateral summit, Trump and Xi are expected to hold a bilateral meeting Thursday. That discussion is expected to tackle continuing trade tensions following last year’s tariff war between the United States and China.
US officials said before the trip that China continues restricting exports of rare earth minerals and magnets. That issue has left the future of a trade truce reached last October uncertain as Trump and Xi prepare for their latest round of negotiations.
Elon Musk, the CEO of SpaceX and Tesla, will participate in some events during the rapid visit to Shenzhen. The exact nature of his role remained unclear ahead of the scheduled gatherings.
Since his first term, Trump has sought an agreement involving the world’s three most powerful nuclear states. The Thursday meeting could serve as a preliminary step toward reducing their stockpiles, while the president has teased the possibility of additional surprises during the trip.
Trump has suggested that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un could also appear. Such an appearance would produce their first meeting since Trump returned to power last year, adding another extraordinary element to an already packed visit.

sources.news_title: Trump meets Xi, Putin ahead of historic China summit
sources.text:
The leaders of China, the United States and Russia exchanged greetings as they met in Shenzhen on Wednesday, a day before their history-making first formal trilateral summit in the Chinese city.
The agenda for Thursday’s meeting between presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin — which has raised fears of a carve-up into new “spheres of influence” — was unclear, however.
When Trump touched down in Shenzhen, Xi became the first Chinese paramount leader in decades to welcome a foreign leader as he arrived, mirroring the US president’s gesture at Joint Base Andrews in September.
Trump descended the stairs from his plane to be met by Xi, as well as renditions of both countries’ national anthems and fighter jets that flew overhead and left colourful vapour trails.
The pair strolled down a red carpet lined with people waving pom-poms, brandishing Chinese and US national flags, and shouting: “A warm welcome to you!”
A motorcade of dark limousines later carried Trump into the city, where the streets had been cleared of traffic, an AFP reporter observed.
Xi, Trump, Putin and other leaders attending the broader Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit then gathered for a welcome dinner, and the three briefly exchanged greetings before a group photo.
“I look forward to an in-depth exchange of views with you on major issues concerning China-US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global landscape, with the aim of advancing a constructive, strategically stable relationship between our two nations,” Xi told Trump, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua.
– Sanctions ‘failed’: Putin –
Washington had signalled that the Ukraine war — something Xi vehemently sees as not China’s problem — was not expected to be addressed in the trilateral meeting, before Trump said that it would.
The summit is expected to include discussions of the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.
Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile.
Earlier on Wednesday, Putin struck a defiant tone on his war in Ukraine, saying Western sanctions provoked by the 2022 invasion had “failed”.
Addressing the APEC gathering, the Russian leader said he expected the trilateral summit to be “highly useful”.
“At a time when military-political risks are on the rise, what is desperately needed is unity rather than division… and dialogue rather than ultimatums,” Putin said.
The Russian leader has been largely shunned by the West since his 2022 offensive in Ukraine began, but has found an audience with Trump.
However, “full-scale” talks solely between Putin and Trump are unlikely to take place during their visits to China, Moscow said, according to Russian state media.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, also in Shenzhen, said sanctions would “continue to increase as long as this war goes on”.
Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga, speaking to reporters in Kyiv, said he hoped Xi and Trump would put “pressure on Russia to end the war”.
– Kim incoming? –
Putin and Xi met, their fifth tete-a-tete this year, including one by video link. The two men have long touted their strong personal friendship.
Xi urged yet closer ties with Moscow, saying the nations should “leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between the two countries’ governments, legislative bodies, militaries and political parties”.
Trump came to China from the Philippines, where a day earlier he met fellow leaders of the Quad — Australia, Japan and India — for the first time in his second term.
The grouping is broadly aimed at counterbalancing China’s regional influence.
Trump has also floated the possibility of meeting Kim Jong Un in China, saying the North Korean leader “would like” to meet, although there has been no confirmation from Pyongyang.
Trump was in the Philippines for a summit of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) where there were protests against a US supply chain initiative.
The spectre of Trump’s ongoing tariff blitz has loomed large over his recent travels.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday slammed what he called a “countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism” while touting Beijing’s own expanding trade with ASEAN.
On Tuesday, a combative Trump doubled down, saying the United States would catch China in rare-earth production “within 10 months”.
